sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the appellants and learned Standing Counsel for the State are present.
2. This delay condonation application has been filed by the appellants for condoning the delay in moving the substitution application for bringing on record the legal heirs of deceased appellant no.
1/3/2 Mohammad Isrial, who has died on 7.11.2021, leaving behind his wife Anjum Bano with two minor children Shabir Shaikh (son) and Ajmin (daughter).

3. Learned counsel for the appellants submitted that the delay occurred because the appeal was dismissed in default and at the time of filing the restoration application, it was noticed by the counsel that the above named appellant has died and immediately thereafter, the substitution application was filed, with delay.
4. An affidavit has been filed in support of the delay condonation application, which is uncontroverted.
5.
The cause shown for filing the substitution application with delay is sufficient.
The delay in filing the substitution application is condoned.
6. Accordingly, the substitution & delay condonation applications are allowed.
7. Learned counsel for the appellants is directed to amend the memo of appeal, accordingly.

Order on Appeal.

1. Heard learned counsel for the appellants and learned Standing Counsel for the State respondents.
2.
Appeal is admitted.

3. The instant appeal under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 has been preferred by the land owners against impugned award and decree dated 7.7.2012 passed by the Additional District Judge, Court No. 14, Varanasi in LAR No. 23 of 2002 [Noor Mohd. (deceased) through LRs & Ors.
Vs. State of U.P. & Ors.], whereby for the land situated in Village Karkhiyanav, Pargana Kolsala,
Tehsil Pindra, District Varanasi, acquired by UPSIDCL for establishing industrial park in District Varanasi, compensation at the rate of Rs. 3,838/- per decimal, besides other statutory benefits admissible under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 has been awarded.

entities.text: Additional District Judge, Court No. 14, Varanasi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for the appellants submitted that the appellants' land situated in Village Karkhiyanav, Pargana Kolsala, Tehsil Pindra, District Varanasi was acquired by the UPSIDCL for establishing industrial park in District Varanasi vide notification under Section 4(1) of the Act dated 21.5.1998.

The appellants' total land measuring 6.77 acre situated in the above village was acquired,
regarding which an award of the Collector was made on 4.8.2001, aggrieved against which, the land owners had preferred reference, which has been disposed by impugned award.

5. Learned counsel for the appellants further submitted that in similar matters, regarding the same land which was acquired by same notification , this Court in First Appeal No. 161 of 2010 (U.P. State Industrial Development Corporation Ltd. Vs. Nazir & Ors.) along with 100 connected First Appeals by order dated 16.4.2018, determined the compensation regarding the land acquired by the UPSIDCL.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellants further submitted that since the matter has attained finality, as such, the land owners in this appeal are also entitled to get compensation at the same rate, at which it has been awarded to the similarly situated land owners, whose land was acquired in Village Karkhiyanav, Pargana Kolsala, Tehsil Pindra, District Varanasi.
9. Learned Standing Counsel for the State respondents has very fairly admitted that the order of this Court passed in the above First Appeals dated 16.4.2018 has attained finality.
10. I have considered the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

11. It is apparent that in this case the land owners' land situated in Village Karkhiyanav, Pargana Kolsala, Tehsil Pindra, District Varanasi has been acquired by the UPSIDCL for establishing industrial park in District Varanasi vide notification under Section 4(1) of the Act dated 21.5.1998.
Regarding the acquired land, the Collector's award was made on 4.8.2001.

Dissatisfied with that award, the land owners challenged it, by filing reference, which has been decided by the impugned award and decree dated 7.7.2012, whereby compensation at the rate of Rs.3,838/- per decimal,
besides other statutory benefits admissible under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 have been awarded to the land owners.

12. It is also apparent that regarding similarly situated land, acquired by same notification dated 21.5.1998, this Court in First Appeal No. 161 of 2010 (U.P. State Industrial Development Corporation Ltd. Vs. Nazir & Ors.) along with 100 connected First Appeals vide order dated 16.4.2018 has awarded compensation for land acquired upto 250 decimal at the rate of Rs. 5,115/-
per decimal and where the acquired land is in excess of 250 decimal, then compensation at the rate of Rs.4,570/- per decimal, has been awarded to the land owners, besides other statutory benefits admissible under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
13.

sentences.text: 14. Accordingly, this appeal is allowed.

Appellants are entitled to get enhanced compensation at the rate of Rs. 4,570/- per decimal for their acquired land, situated in Village Karkhiyanav, Pargana Kolsala, Tehsil Pindra, District Varanasi, along with 30% solatium, additional compensation @ 12%
per annum and interest under Section 28, as provided under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
15.

The instant appeal was filed on 19.11.2012 which was dismissed for want of prosecution on 26.11.2018, and the appeal was restored on 17.7.2025 and further, the deficiency of court fees was made good on 21.7.2025, as such, the appellants are not entitled to get interest on the enhanced compensation for the period 19.11.2012 to 21.7.2025.
16.
However, in the facts and circumstances of the case, the parties shall bear their respective costs.
17. Office is directed to prepare the decree accordingly.
